title: Exhaust System — 3.7L Duratec
introduction:
An exhaust system is more than the bit that gives the car its voice. I follow it as a working route: gases leave the engine, the catalytic converters reduce pollutants, and the muffler assembly reduces noise before discharge. The underbody resonator belongs to that assembly, while isolators support it.

This overview explains the layout and the conditions that can damage it. It also identifies shield checks and fastener rules. It does not supply the access, removal, installation or tightening details needed for a complete repair; use the relevant component service procedure for that work.

edits.why: The component descriptions explain the route; the notices and care rules explain what can undermine it.

edits.text: NOTICE: Never use leaded fuel in a vehicle equipped with a catalytic converter. Repeated misfueling deposits lead in the converter and can completely blanket the catalyst. Lead also reacts with platinum to chemically poison the catalyst. Continued use can destroy the catalyst and make the converter useless. Lead can also solidify the catalyst, causing excessive exhaust back pressure and possibly damaging the engine.
edits.why: Lead contamination threatens both the converter's chemical function and free passage of exhaust gases.

edits.text: NOTICE: Misfiring or an over-rich fuel/air mixture can produce converter temperatures of 1,100°C (2,012°F) or above. Such heat will sinter—fuse together—or burn the ceramic substrate, destroying the catalytic converter. Do not continue operating the vehicle if the engine misfires, loses power or develops other unusual operating conditions, including overheating or backfiring.
edits.why: These symptoms require stopping vehicle operation because continued running can damage the converter.

edits.text: NOTICE: Do not use oil- or grease-based lubricants on the exhaust isolators. These lubricants can deteriorate the rubber and allow an isolator to separate from its exhaust hanger bracket during vehicle operation.
edits.why: Rubber compatibility matters to the security of the exhaust mounting.

edits.text: The exhaust system gives spent gases a route out of the engine and reduces engine noise by passing those gases through catalytic converters and a muffler assembly. The converters also reduce air pollutants.
edits.why: The same route has separate chemical and acoustic jobs; that distinction helps explain the components below.

edits.text: An LH one-piece catalytic converter manifold mounted to the LH exhaust manifold.
An RH one-piece catalytic converter manifold mounted to the RH exhaust manifold.
An underbody resonator that forms part of the muffler and tailpipe assembly.
edits.why: This identifies the resonator's place within the assembly rather than presenting it as an unrelated underbody part.

edits.text: A muffler and tailpipe assembly supported by isolators.
edits.why: The isolators connect the assembly to its mounting brackets and bring the rubber-protection notice into play.

edits.text: The catalytic converter acts as a gas reactor in the emissions-control system. It speeds heat-producing chemical reactions between components of the exhaust gases, reducing air pollutants.
edits.why: I think of this as the exhaust's chemistry department: the catalyst helps the reactions happen as gases pass through.

edits.text: The catalytic converter's internal catalyst structure uses a ceramic substrate.
edits.why: This identifies the ceramic material affected by the excessive-temperature notice.

edits.text: The catalytic converter is designed for a long service life and requires no routine maintenance.
edits.why: Its maintenance-free design does not remove the need to avoid damaging fuel and abnormal engine operation.

edits.text: Sound insulators and shields attached to the underbody and exhaust system protect the vehicle from exhaust heat. Inspect them regularly for dents and incorrect positioning. Install a new insulator or shield if it is damaged or shows deterioration. The insulators and shields for the muffler, muffler pipe, resonator and catalytic converter pipe are installed separately.
edits.why: Their position is part of their protective function. This overview identifies what to look for and when replacement is required; it does not teach physical access or replacement.

edits.text: Where the relevant service procedure requires an exhaust fastener to be discarded, install a new one. Also discard damaged or heavily corroded fasteners and replace them as needed. Some exhaust fasteners use a prevailing-torque design; use only new replacement fasteners with the same part number as the originals. During reassembly, tighten the fasteners to the specified torque to retain the exhaust components correctly.
edits.why: Correct retention depends on the replacement rule as well as tightening. Obtain the specific discard instructions and torque from the component procedure before reassembly.
